request.spec:
When I come back later and open a sheet by its name, I want to see the people and all their
numbers and values exactly as I left them, even after the page has been refreshed.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for this implementation's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
When I come back later and open a sheet by its name, I want to see the people and all their
numbers and values exactly as I left them, even after the page has been refreshed.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Both tests in the spec pass when run with `bin/e2e`: the test that reopens a sheet after a page refresh, and the new one for opening an unknown sheet.

Recalling a sheet already worked. Sheets, their people and all their values were already saved on the server, so opening a sheet by name after a refresh shows everything as it was left. The part that was missing was what happens when you open a name that doesn't exist. Before, that showed an empty list that looked just like a real empty sheet.

**What I changed:**
- **Server:** a new `GET /api/sheets/{id}` endpoint returns the sheet, or a 404 if no sheet has that id (`SheetController.java`). `PersonService` has a new `sheetExists` method that it uses.
- **Front end:**
  - `PeopleService.sheetExists()` turns that 404 into `false`.
  - When you open a named sheet, `People` now checks whether it exists. If it doesn't, the page shows a `sheet-missing` message: *No sheet named "…" exists yet.*

You can still add a person to a sheet name that doesn't exist yet. That creates the sheet, as it did before, and the missing message goes away once the list reloads.
